'''Michel Pouchard''' (born 23 January, 1938 in [[Avrillé-les-Ponceaux]]) is a French [[chemist]] specialising in the [[Physicochemistry|physico-chemistry]] of inorganic solids.

== Biography ==
After studying at the David high school in [[Angers]] and at the faculties of science at [[University of Rennes]] and [[University of Bordeaux]],<ref name="espci2">[https://sho.spip.espci.fr/spip.php?article20 « Entretien avec Michel Pouchard »], par [[Pierre Tissier|Pierre Teissier]], 20 septembre 2004, Sciences : [[histoire orale]]</ref> Michel Pouchard specializes in the physico-chemistry of inorganic solids: oxides of [[transition metal]]s, electronic properties ([[magnetism]], [[Metal-insulator transition|insulation-to-metal transition]]) and [[electrochemistry]] (materials for energy, membranes, electrodes for SOFC [[fuel]] cells in particular), [[nanocrystalline silicon]]) and in the science of functional materials.

Trainee then research associate at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] from 1960 to 1967 (director of the materials technology dissemination department at the CNRS from 1975 to 1984), he was a lecturer at the Faculty of Sciences, [[University of Bordeaux]] from 1967 to 1970, then professor at the [[University of Bordeaux]] I from 1970 to 1992 (professor emeritus from 2004). From 1992 to 2002, he was a professor at the [[Institut Universitaire de France|Institut universitaire de France]] (of which he was a director from 1993 to 1997).<ref name="espci2"/>

He was elected a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]] on 16 November 1992.<ref name="ads">{{Cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Pouchard_Michel.htm |title=Michel Pouchard - les Membres de l'Académie des sciences |access-date=2019-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221003548/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Pouchard_Michel.htm |archive-date=2014-12-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is also a member of the Academy of Technologies,<ref name="techno">{{Cite web |url=http://www.academie-technologies.fr/en/members/250-michel-pouchard |title=Académie des technologies |access-date=2019-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160410173746/http://www.academie-technologies.fr/en/members/250-michel-pouchard |archive-date=2016-04-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the French Society of Chemistry,<ref name="scf2">{{cite web |url=http://www.societechimiquedefrance.fr/1/breve/la-scf-en-video.html |title=La SCF en vidéo ! - Société Chimique de France |website=www.societechimiquedefrance.fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221002907/http://www.societechimiquedefrance.fr/1/breve/la-scf-en-video.html |archive-date=2014-12-21}} </ref> the [[Academia Europaea|Academia europaea]] (1998)<ref>{{cite web|title=Academia europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pouchard_Michel|publication-date=}}</ref> and the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina Academy]] (Germany) (2000).

== Publications ==
Michel Pouchard is the author of nearly 400 articles published in the best journals in solid-state chemistry and materials science and some fifteen patents.<ref>{{cite web|title=Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.fr/scholar?hl=fr&as_sdt=0%2C5&q=Michel+pouchard&btnG=|publication-date=}}</ref><ref name="ads" />

== Distinctions ==

=== Prices ===
Langevin Prize of the French Academy of sciences (1977)

=== Decorations ===
* Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'honneur]].
* Commandeur of the [[Ordre national du Mérite|Ordre national du mérite]]. He was promoted to officier on May 15, 2017, and then obtained the rank of commandeur by decree on November 18, 2017.
* Commandeur of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques]].
